evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: `manager_restarted` only proves that the manager PID and invocation ID changed. A guest reboot also changes both, so a reboot can satisfy this check and then a later reboot can satisfy `boot_id_changed`, allowing the feasibility run to pass without ever exercising a manager-only restart. Requiring nonempty and equal boot IDs around the manager before/after snapshots is a routine correctness repair to the existing check, not an enlargement of scope.
